experience.explanation: Daytime finals on an open-air range with about 2,000 seats. Home-crowd energy can build, but the shoot lacks prime-time spectacle.

starPower.explanation: Hancock chasing a fifth straight gold, plus world champions Hansen and Jiang and 2025 champion Simonton. A dense, recognizable field.

uniqueness.explanation: Hancock's bid for a fifth gold would be a Games first, and the eight-athlete final is new. The venue is fresh for skeet finals.

demand.explanation: Final-day skeet with a home-favorite storyline draws strong interest. Mid-tier sport demand, lifted by the Hancock narrative.

scorecard.overall: Skeet medal day at Whittier Narrows, with gold decided in both the men's and women's eight-athlete finals. Hancock's fifth-gold chase and the home crowd make it the marquee shotgun session, though the daytime timing keeps the energy measured.

significance.explanation: Gold-medal final in the men's 50m rifle three positions, with the new standing-plus-elimination format deciding the podium.

experience.explanation: A morning-to-early-afternoon session in a calm hall, which suits focused fans but has less prime-time energy.

starPower.explanation: Paris 2024 champion Liu Yukun and world-record holder Zhang Changhong give the field real recognition.

uniqueness.explanation: The standing-only redesign for 2028 gives this final a new shape, though the event itself is well established.

demand.explanation: A daytime final in a small hall keeps demand solid, with China and India fans driving interest.

scorecard.overall: The men's 50m rifle three positions final, now standing-only after kneeling and prone merge. Paris 2024 champion Liu Yukun leads a field that can swing on a single shot.

significance.explanation: Gold-medal final in the women's 50m rifle three positions, where the standing-only format puts all the pressure on the last shots.

experience.explanation: A morning-to-early-afternoon final in a hushed hall, with a close finish giving daytime sessions their tension.

starPower.explanation: Paris 2024 champion Chiara Leone and Doha gold medalist Aleksandra Stojadinovic headline a field with strong recognition.

uniqueness.explanation: Standing-only final format is new for 2028, which sets this apart from the standard women's rifle event.

demand.explanation: Daytime final with a strong pool of recognizable names, so it should sell steadily without being the hardest ticket.

scorecard.overall: The women's 50m rifle three positions final, now decided by standing plus elimination. Paris 2024 champion Chiara Leone returns to a field where a single standing shot can swing the medals.

significance.explanation: Opening trap qualification where a clean day decides who makes the top eight. Stakes are real, but no medals yet.

experience.explanation: Morning-to-afternoon trap at a public range with expanded seating. Easy to follow targets from the stands, though low on energy.

starPower.explanation: Qualification fields include world-level shooters, but few globally known names are guaranteed. Recent form varies widely.

uniqueness.explanation: Routine trap qualification in an established format. One of several shooting sessions during the Games.

demand.explanation: Early trap qualification at a good venue. Still expected to sell, but less competitive than the finals.

scorecard.overall: Trap opens with qualification at Whittier Narrows, where shooters need steady scores to reach the eight-athlete final. It is a practical way to see the sport up close before medal day.

significance.explanation: Qualification stages decide who advances to the finals, so the stakes are real but not medal-deciding.

experience.explanation: A long daytime session in a quiet hall, with the stages running from morning to late afternoon.

starPower.explanation: Manu Bhaker and Clement Bessaguet may compete, though the field is mostly national-level shooters at this stage.

uniqueness.explanation: Qualification stages of established pistol events at a convention-hall range, so this is routine shooting format.

demand.explanation: An early prelim session of a niche event, so seats are easier to book than the finals while Games scarcity still applies.

scorecard.overall: Qualification stages for the men's rapid fire and women's 25m pistol, set up for Sunday's finals. It is a good way to see the sport up close, with fewer seats than the finals.

significance.explanation: Two gold-medal trap finals with eight finalists each. Two medal sets are settled in one session.

experience.explanation: Shooters sit close to the stands, so the call, shot and crowd reaction arrive quickly. Strong atmosphere in a daytime slot.

starPower.explanation: Paris 2024 champions Hales and Ruano may compete, but neither is guaranteed a place. Glasnovic and Hinton add depth.

uniqueness.explanation: Standard trap medal finals with a returning Paris champion. The eight-athlete format adds a small twist.

demand.explanation: Two medal finals in a mid-tier sport with Paris storylines. Strong interest from trap fans and Guatemalan and British supporters.

scorecard.overall: Trap medals are decided here in separate men's and women's finals, each with eight shooters. The stands sit behind the line, and Paris 2024 champions Hales and Ruano may return to defend their titles.

significance.explanation: Two pistol medal finals on one day, including the rapid fire final that grows to eight shooters for 2028.

experience.explanation: A full-day finals session that runs into the evening, with rapid-fire strings giving the hall its most dramatic atmosphere.

starPower.explanation: Yang Jiin, the Paris 2024 champion, and Florian Peter and Clement Bessaguet of the rapid fire field bring strong recognition.

uniqueness.explanation: The eight-shooter rapid fire final is new for 2028, which gives this session a fresh format.

demand.explanation: Two medal finals on a Sunday with high-profile names, so the seats should go quickly.

scorecard.overall: Men's rapid fire final and women's 25m pistol final on the same Sunday, with the rapid fire field growing to eight shooters. Yang Jiin and Florian Peter are the names to watch in this high-energy session.

significance.explanation: Gold-medal mixed team final where four teams shoot together. Every shot can change the medal order.

experience.explanation: Daytime mixed team shooting at a range with stands near the line. The four-team format gives a clear storyline, though the day runs long.

starPower.explanation: Mixed teams rarely feature globally known names. Eller and Downs are rising trap names, and there are few household faces.

uniqueness.explanation: Brand new event replacing mixed skeet, with a new four-team shoot-off format. A first-ever medal final for this pairing.

demand.explanation: A new team event with an unfamiliar format and a fresh storyline. Trap and skeet fans will want to see how it works.

scorecard.overall: Mixed team trap makes its debut, replacing mixed skeet, and the top four teams all shoot together in one medal final. Expect a new format and a storyline that plays out in real time from the stands.

significance.explanation: Preliminary round where the 22 women skaters fight for a final place. Real stakes for every rider, but no medals decided tonight.

experience.explanation: Evening start in the open-air Sepulveda Basin gives a relaxed, close-up view of the rails and ledges, though the prelim pace is steadier than the final.

starPower.explanation: Top names like Yoshizawa, Akama, Leal and Covell may be in the field, but early rounds don't guarantee the headline riders show up.

uniqueness.explanation: Early round of a returning sport, and the first skateboarding session at the Games. Important as an opener, but it is one of several preliminaries.

demand.explanation: Preliminary of a popular sport with an evening slot. Expected to sell well, but easier to book than the finals.

scorecard.overall: The women's street prelim opens the skateboarding program under the Sepulveda Basin evening lights. Japan's depth and Leal's return make the field worth watching as riders chase the final.

significance.explanation: Men's street preliminary where all 22 skaters compete for a spot in the final. The stakes are real, but the medals come later.

experience.explanation: Late-morning daytime start with bright sun in the basin. Good for watching the whole field, though it lacks prime-time energy.

starPower.explanation: Horigome, Shirai, Sasaki and the Japanese contingent are strong draws, and Huston is aiming to compete. Early-round attendance is not guaranteed for the top names.

uniqueness.explanation: Men's preliminary of a returning sport. It is a non-medal round, so it is less rare than the final that follows.

demand.explanation: Morning preliminary with a deep, popular men's field. It should sell, but it is easier to secure than the evening final.

scorecard.overall: A daytime men's street prelim sets up the night's final with a deep field led by Japan's rising stars. U.S. skaters on the card bring a home-crowd edge if they advance.

significance.explanation: Medal final in a returning sport, deciding the women's street podium. The last-trick format keeps every run meaningful.

experience.explanation: Prime-time 8:30 pm final under the lights at an open-air venue. Crowd reactions to each landed trick make it one of the sport's strongest nights.

starPower.explanation: Yoshizawa, Oda, Matsumoto, Leal and Covell give the final several recognizable names with recent world-title pedigree.

uniqueness.explanation: Medal round of a returning sport in a purpose-built venue at a rare Games moment. The first women's street gold of the program is decided here.

demand.explanation: Evening final with a heavily tracked Japanese storyline. Strong demand, though a mid-tier finals slot limits it below the marquee sessions.

scorecard.overall: The women's street final is the evening headliner, with medals decided under the lights in the Sepulveda Basin. Japan's depth and Leal's comeback story make the last-trick finish worth the ticket.

significance.explanation: Gold-medal final in a non-marquee sport, with eight skaters deciding the title on their last trick. Stakes are high even though the field is small.

experience.explanation: Evening final at 8:30 pm under lights in the Sepulveda Basin. High-energy street skating at a temporary open-air course gives it a strong live feel.

starPower.explanation: Defending champion Horigome, world No. 1 Sora Shirai and two-time world champion Sasaki Toa are all in contention. Several globally known names could make the final.

uniqueness.explanation: Skateboarding's first Games medal final in the San Fernando Valley, on a course built only for 2028. The return to Southern California roots makes it a one-off.

demand.explanation: Evening medal session in Los Angeles for a sport with a large local following. Expect strong competition for seats despite the smaller, temporary venue.

scorecard.overall: A gold-medal street final under the lights in the Sepulveda Basin, with Horigome and the Japanese podium contenders headlining. The first Games events in the San Fernando Valley and the sport's Southern California roots give it added pull.

significance.explanation: Preliminary round where skaters are fighting for advancement rather than medals. Real stakes for every rider, but the medal decision comes later.

experience.explanation: Late-morning session in a fresh temporary bowl. Daylight skating is still a live Games experience, just without the prime-time energy.

starPower.explanation: Early-round session where Palmer and Bijueska may or may not drop in. Top riders often compete in prelims, so the names are possible but not assured.

uniqueness.explanation: Early round of a returning sport at a venue built only for these Games. Not a once-in-a-lifetime session, but a rare chance to see the field first.

demand.explanation: Morning prelim with an easier path to a ticket than the finals. Park skateboarding still draws strong interest in Southern California.

scorecard.overall: A morning men's park prelim at Valley Complex 2 that sorts 22 skaters into the final. Palmer and Bijueska are in the frame, and it is a relaxed way to see the field before the medal sessions.

significance.explanation: Qualifying round in which the cut to the final is tight. Every rider is competing for advancement, though no medals are decided here.

experience.explanation: Evening session with a lively crowd around the bowl. Strong energy for a skate event, though the temporary venue keeps it a notch below a showpiece stage.

starPower.explanation: Hasegawa, Brown and Trew are all likely in the field. Early rounds still carry the sport's top names, though not every favourite is guaranteed to ride.

uniqueness.explanation: Early women's park round at a new venue. A chance to see the form leaders on the way to the final, but one of several rounds of the sport.

demand.explanation: Evening slot in a popular sport with a stacked field. Expect strong interest, though it is less competitive to book than the medal session.

scorecard.overall: An evening women's park prelim with a deep field of recent world and X Games names. It is a good first look at the form before the final, and the evening crowd gives it a lively feel.

significance.explanation: Gold-medal final in a non-marquee sport. Palmer is going for a third straight Games title, and the medals are decided in this session.

experience.explanation: Prime-time evening final with a loud crowd and a long run of high-risk tricks. The venue is temporary rather than iconic, which holds the score back slightly.

starPower.explanation: Palmer, Bijueska and Schaar all have strong credentials and are likely to contend. The final line-up depends on qualification, so the names are not yet locked.

uniqueness.explanation: Medal round of a returning sport with a possible three-peat for Palmer. Rare, medal-deciding and only held once every four years.

demand.explanation: Men's park final in prime evening slot. Competition for these seats will be intense because the medal decision is the marquee moment of the event.

scorecard.overall: The men's park gold-medal final on Wednesday evening, with Palmer seeking a third straight title against Bijueska and the Asuncion podium. A single clean run can decide it, so expect a tense 75 minutes.

significance.explanation: Gold-medal final in a non-marquee sport. Paris 2024 was decided by less than a point, and the Games crown is still up for grabs.

experience.explanation: Thursday prime-time final with a close-up atmosphere around the bowl. The temporary venue is a step below an iconic stage, but the spectacle is high.

starPower.explanation: Hasegawa, Brown and Trew give the final several recognizable contenders. Qualification will set the final field, but the medal picture is full of recent champions.

uniqueness.explanation: Women's park medal final where the event has only two prior Games champions to draw from. A rare, once-in-a-lifetime decision.

demand.explanation: Women's park final in prime evening slot with several top medal contenders. Expect demand to be strong for these seats.

scorecard.overall: The women's park gold-medal final on Thursday evening, with Hasegawa, Brown and Trew among the leading contenders. Paris 2024 was settled by 0.87 points across the podium, so the final should be close.

significance.explanation: Round of 16 opener where a single loss ends a campaign. Real stakes for every player, though no medals are decided tonight.

experience.explanation: Evening squash on a temporary court set against Hollywood facades. The 7:30 pm start gives a lively first-night feel.

starPower.explanation: Mostafa Asal and Amina Orfi top the rankings, but early-round squash draws do not guarantee the biggest names will be on court.

uniqueness.explanation: Opening night of squash's Games debut, with a first-ever Round of 16 at the venue. Still an early round rather than a medal session.

demand.explanation: Brand-new sport on its first night, so interest is building. Expect solid but less competitive booking than marquee sessions.

scorecard.overall: Squash's first night on the Games program opens a single-elimination Round of 16 under the lights at Universal Studios. Top Egyptian and Malaysian names give it credibility, though the early-round format keeps the stakes lower than the medal sessions.

significance.explanation: Second night of Round of 16 matches where every loser is out. The stakes are real, but no medals are on the line.

experience.explanation: Evening session on the backlot stands with an open-air, studio-set backdrop. The energy is good, but it is a smaller stage than the medal rounds.

starPower.explanation: Egypt's two-athlete cap means some top-ranked Egyptians will be absent, which thins the star quotient of the early draw.

uniqueness.explanation: Another evening of the same format in the sport's debut week. Sits between routine and special, given the new-sport context.

demand.explanation: Early-round sessions of a new sport at a temporary venue draw steady demand, though it is easier to book than the finals.

scorecard.overall: Night two of the Round of 16 brings four more single-elimination matches on the Universal backlot. The two-per-country cap means Egypt's depth in the rankings will not all reach the court, so expect some mismatches in the early rounds.

significance.explanation: Third night of Round of 16, with the field still settling. Each result has real consequences for qualifying athletes.

experience.explanation: Late-evening squash in temporary stands against Courthouse Square, with a distinctive film-set backdrop.

starPower.explanation: English brothers Marwan and Mohamed ElShorbagy are ranked near the top, but early rounds may or may not feature them.

uniqueness.explanation: Early round in a sport debuting on the program, so each match is a first. Routine within the squash schedule.

demand.explanation: Early-round squash at a new, distinctive venue will sell steadily, though not at finals-level pressure.

scorecard.overall: The bracket keeps thinning toward the quarterfinals with four more Round of 16 matches. The final qualifying place per gender is still open, so the draw may shift before the session begins.

significance.explanation: Final night of the Round of 16, sending eight players per draw into the quarterfinals. Advancement is at stake, not medals.

experience.explanation: Late-evening session on the backlot, with the film-set backdrop adding atmosphere to the squash action.

starPower.explanation: Paul Coll and Diego Elias are both in the mix, but early-round appearances from top-tier players are not guaranteed.

uniqueness.explanation: Completes the Round of 16 in a new sport. The session matters for the bracket, though it is not a medal round.

demand.explanation: Closing night of the early rounds draws steady interest. Expect easier access than the semifinal and final sessions.

scorecard.overall: The Round of 16 wraps up tonight, completing the eight quarterfinal places in both draws. Egyptian and international players will be on court here, but the early-round setting keeps the medal drama for later nights.

significance.explanation: Quarterfinal knockouts where winners reach the medal round and losers exit without a medal. Serious stakes, one step short of the semifinals.

experience.explanation: Quarterfinal evening on the backlot with louder crowds expected. Strong energy for a new-sport session.

starPower.explanation: Mostafa Asal, a two-time world champion, and other top men and women headline the quarterfinal draw.

uniqueness.explanation: First quarterfinal of squash at the Games, so the storylines are fresh. It is still a stage short of the medal matches.

demand.explanation: Quarterfinals of a debut sport with an Egyptian storyline attract strong interest and tight booking.

scorecard.overall: The quarterfinals begin, and the first four matches send winners into the medal round. Two-time champion Asal and the Egyptian depth in both draws make this the first night of squash's real storylines.

significance.explanation: Second quarterfinal night completing the semifinal lineups. Winners reach a medal match, and losers leave without one.

experience.explanation: Evening quarterfinal on the film backlot with a cinematic setting. The tension builds as the draw narrows.

starPower.explanation: Paul Coll and Diego Elias, the top non-Egyptian men, are in contention alongside Malaysia's Subramaniam.

uniqueness.explanation: Completes the squash quarterfinals in a debut sport. Historic weight comes from the first Games medal pathway.

demand.explanation: Second quarterfinal session with multiple recognizable names. Demand will be high from fans chasing the first medal positions.

scorecard.overall: This session completes the men's and women's semifinal lineups, with Coll and Elias among the players who could push through. Every result here moves a squash athlete closer to the first Games medal in the sport's history.

significance.explanation: Women's semifinals in a smaller sport. Winners go to gold, losers to bronze, so medals are assured for both.

experience.explanation: Late-evening semifinal on the backlot with an intense crowd between rallies. Strong atmosphere for a single medal-decisive night.

starPower.explanation: Amina Orfi, Nouran Gohar and Nour El Sherbini have all won recent world titles, with Olivia Weaver as a potential home contender.

uniqueness.explanation: Women's semifinals decide the first women's squash medals at the Games. A once-only medal round for a debut sport.

demand.explanation: Semifinal session with a guaranteed medal for each loser. Strong draw for fans of the sport and the Egyptian stars.

scorecard.overall: The women's semifinals determine the first medal pairings in squash at the Games, with each loser guaranteed a bronze match. Egyptian world champions headline the lineup, and the 8:30 pm start builds toward a late finish.

significance.explanation: Men's semifinals in a smaller sport with guaranteed bronze for each loser. Winners reach gold, a major stake.

experience.explanation: Evening semifinal on the backlot with the 11:15 pm finish. The format delivers tension within two matches.

starPower.explanation: Mostafa Asal, Paul Coll and Diego Elias are all contenders for these two semifinal places.

uniqueness.explanation: Men's semifinals decide the first men's squash medal pairings at the Games. A rare, once-only medal stage.

demand.explanation: Two high-profile matches in a late-evening session. Demand is strong with Egyptian and international names involved.

scorecard.overall: The men's semifinals decide who plays for gold and who heads to bronze. Asal and Coll lead the favorites, and with Egypt limited to two entries, a non-Egyptian semifinalist is very likely.

significance.explanation: Women's bronze and gold medal matches decide the first women's squash medals at the Games. Gold is the top prize in the sport.

experience.explanation: Late-night medal session on the backlot with a charged atmosphere. Strong energy for the sport's first podium.

starPower.explanation: Orfi, El Sherbini, Gohar, Subramaniam and Weaver give the podium recognizable names.

uniqueness.explanation: The first women's squash medals in Games history, decided on a film-set court. Once-in-a-lifetime for the sport.

demand.explanation: Medal session of a debut sport with a historic first podium. Expect heavy competition for seats.

scorecard.overall: The first women's squash medals in Games history are decided tonight, with bronze followed by gold. Egypt's recent world champions lead the field, but the two-per-country cap leaves room for Malaysia or the United States to break through.

significance.explanation: Men's bronze and gold medal matches decide the first men's squash medals. The gold is the sport's marquee prize at the Games.

experience.explanation: Closing-night medal session on the backlot, with a late finish and a celebratory feel. Strong energy throughout.

starPower.explanation: Asal, the two-time world champion, along with Coll and Elias, provides a top-tier headline matchup for the medals.

uniqueness.explanation: The closing squash session of the Games and the sport's first men's medals. A once-only pairing of stakes and setting.

demand.explanation: Closing night of the sport with the first men's medals on the line. Among the most sought-after squash sessions.

scorecard.overall: The closing session decides squash's first men's medals, with bronze followed by gold on the Universal backlot. Asal is the projected favorite, but Coll and Elias have beaten top Egyptians in major finals, so the podium should include at least one non-Egyptian.

significance.explanation: Opening round for both genders, where every surfer is fighting for a place in the next round rather than for medal positions.

experience.explanation: Early 7:30 AM start on a natural beach break. Watchable surfing, but the morning slot takes away some of the energy.

starPower.explanation: Top names may be scattered through the heats, but many spots will go to qualifiers and lesser-known surfers.

uniqueness.explanation: First look at Lower Trestles for the full field, which gives it a fresh feel even though the format is standard.

demand.explanation: Round 1 surfing at a notable venue. It should sell steadily, though it's easier to book than the medal days.

scorecard.overall: Opening morning of surfing at Lower Trestles, with men's and women's Round 1 heats on the cobblestone point. It's an early look at the field, so the attraction is the wave and the chance to spot emerging names before the bracket tightens.

significance.explanation: Round 2 is a second chance for surfers who slipped early, so the stakes are real but still short of medal-deciding.

experience.explanation: Sunday morning heats in a temporary beachside setup. Good surfing, though the timing keeps it from feeling like a headline session.

starPower.explanation: Recent Trestles winners could be in the water, but the field is still being filled by qualifiers and surfers from smaller nations.

uniqueness.explanation: A second-round heat at a break with a recent Championship Tour history. It's a regular round, but the venue gives it a local feel.

demand.explanation: Mid-tier round at a respected venue. Expect strong interest from surf fans, with more availability than the finals.

scorecard.overall: Sunday's Round 2 heats bring the men's and women's fields down to a smaller group at Lower Trestles. It's a useful session for seeing how the cobblestone A-frames suit the surfers who survived the first round.

significance.explanation: Round 3 is a prelim where surfers are still fighting to reach the quarterfinals. Real stakes, but not yet medal-deciding.

experience.explanation: Monday morning heats at a natural beach venue. The surf quality is strong, but the early start limits the atmosphere.

starPower.explanation: Several recognizable names, including the 2026 tour leaders and Paris 2024 bronze medalist, could still be alive in the bracket.

uniqueness.explanation: Standard prelim format, but the field is narrowing, so the heats feel more like a preview of the medal day.

demand.explanation: Round 3 is a solid session at a respected venue, and it will still sell well, though it's easier to get than medal day.

scorecard.overall: Monday's Round 3 heats are where the field gets tighter and the big names start to matter more. Three-surfer national teams and tour rivalries make the heat draws worth watching at Lower Trestles.

significance.explanation: Quarterfinals, semifinals, and both medal matches on one day. Paris 2024 champions and recent world title holders compete for medals.

experience.explanation: Full day at a top-tier natural break, though there are no permanent grandstands and the timing runs through the morning and afternoon.

starPower.explanation: Defending champions Vaast and Marks are joined by Medina, Moore, Picklum, and Colapinto, so the star list is deep.

uniqueness.explanation: Multi-medal surfing day at Lower Trestles is a rare pairing of the 2028 Games and a famous break, and it happens only once.

demand.explanation: Medal day with defending champions and home-water favorites. Expect the most competitive ticket demand of the surfing program.

scorecard.overall: Medal day at Lower Trestles puts the quarterfinals, semifinals, bronze, and gold matches into one session on the same break. Defending champions and San Clemente locals on home water make it the strongest surfing ticket of the 2028 Games.

significance.explanation: Opening technical routine of the duet program. Scores feed the medal total, but this is a round where advancement and placing are still in play.

experience.explanation: Late-morning open-air pool on the waterfront. Good for watching the first routines of the Games, though without prime-time energy.

starPower.explanation: Austria's Alexandri twins and China's new Lin Yanjun and Xu Huiyan are the names to watch, but top pairs' appearances are not fully confirmed.

uniqueness.explanation: The opening session of the sport's program, and the first look at the new Long Beach pool. Routine within a multi-day event.

demand.explanation: A short session that is easier to book than the medal sessions, though it should still sell well with the sport's first Games outing.

scorecard.overall: The opening women's duet technical routine sets the first scores of the artistic swimming program. Early technical marks from top pairs matter, and the session gives a clear first view of the open-air Long Beach pool.

significance.explanation: Duet medal session, where the free score settles the gold. Stakes are high for the pairs chasing China's Paris 2024 title.

experience.explanation: Late-morning slot at an open-air pool close to the water. Music and synchronized rhythm carry well, but it is not an evening session.

starPower.explanation: Shortman and Thorpe's return and China's Lin and Xu give the final real recognition. Paris 2024 duet champions have not been confirmed.

uniqueness.explanation: A duet medal decided in a well-established sport at a new venue. The rarity lies in the Long Beach setting rather than the format.

demand.explanation: Medal decider in a mid-tier sport at a purpose-built venue. Likely to sell quickly among fans of the sport.

scorecard.overall: The women's duet free routine decides the duet medals, adding to Tuesday's technical score. Chinese and British pairs lead the contenders, and the late-morning session carries strong medal stakes in the open-air pool.

significance.explanation: Preliminary technical routine for the team event. Teams are competing for placement, but the medals come later.

experience.explanation: Short late-morning session with eight-member teams in formation. Easy to follow for a first-time viewer at an open-air venue.

starPower.explanation: China's team lineup and the neutral-athlete squads are the draw. Individual star names are less confirmed at this stage.

uniqueness.explanation: Team technical in a format that now includes men. A standard routine round, though the first team event with men in the new format.

demand.explanation: Early round in a niche team event. Still expected to sell, but easier to book than the finals.

scorecard.overall: The team technical routine is the first of three scores that make up the team medal. Eight-swimmer formations are easy to see at the open-air pool, and China's team is the headline.

significance.explanation: Team free preliminary, where routine scores start to reshuffle the standings. Real stakes, but the medals come later.

experience.explanation: Friday late-morning slot with a themed routine filling much of the pool. Good for watching choreography in the open air.

starPower.explanation: China has won the team free every year since 2022, but the field's stars are not confirmed. Japan and Spain are the other names to watch.

uniqueness.explanation: A standard team routine round. Its link to the sport's 1984 Los Angeles debut adds some local interest.

demand.explanation: Early team round that should still draw a full crowd. Easier to book than the medal session.

scorecard.overall: The team free routine is the second of the three team scores and offers the most room for creative choreography. The session returns the sport to Los Angeles, where it debuted in 1984.

significance.explanation: Team medal final where the acrobatic routine decides the podium. China's defense of its Paris 2024 gold is on the line.

experience.explanation: Late-morning closing session of the sport. Lifts and throws are visible in the open-air pool, though not in prime time.

starPower.explanation: China's Lin and Xu appeared in the 2026 acrobatic win. The team field is strong but lacks many household names.

uniqueness.explanation: Closing session of the sport, with the team gold decided on the final acrobatic routine. The format is established, but the context is distinct.

demand.explanation: Final medal session in a mid-tier sport at a purpose-built venue. Likely to sell well among fans of the sport.

scorecard.overall: The team acrobatic routine closes artistic swimming and decides the team medals. Throws and lifts can reshape the podium in a single routine, and China's title defense is the central storyline.

significance.explanation: Heats only, so these swimmers are fighting for advancement rather than medals. Real stakes for every entrant in the first morning session.

experience.explanation: Early Sunday-style morning start in the 9:30 slot. The pool and the ring-shaped video board still make it a memorable first look at the venue.
